html:
The Wenatchi are an Interior Salish people of the Wenatchee River valley in central Washington state, where the river meets the Columbia. Their own name, np̓əšqʷáw̓səxʷ, is often written P'squosa. They gathered at fishing sites on the Wenatchee and Icicle rivers for the salmon runs, and dug roots and picked berries in the Cascade foothills.

In the Yakama treaty of 1855 the Wenatchi were counted among the Yakama peoples, and the treaty promised them a small fishing reservation at Wenatshapam that was never set up. Most Wenatchi later moved to the Colville reservation, where they are one of the Confederated Tribes. Neighbours: Entiat, Chelan and Sinkiuse.
